editions.title: This weekend on E-Grid
editions.intro: Two rounds on the calendar this week, from 13 to 16 November. The World Rally Championship reaches Jeddah for Saudi Arabia's fourteenth round, while NHRA Drag Racing closes its season with the Finals at Pomona in California.

items.headline: Rally Saudi Arabia
items.body: The World Rally Championship heads to Jeddah for Rally Saudi Arabia on Saturday 14 November. The season's fourteenth round runs over the desert stages around the city.

items.headline: NHRA Finals
items.body: The Pomona Dragstrip in California hosts the NHRA Finals on Sunday 15 November. It closes the drag racing calendar for the year, with drivers lining up at the familiar California track.

editions.title: This weekend on E-Grid
editions.intro: Two rounds this week across the World Rally Championship and NHRA Drag Racing, with the Saudi Arabian event on Saturday and the season finale in California on Sunday. Here is what to expect from each over the coming days.

items.headline: Rally Saudi Arabia
items.body: The World Rally Championship reaches Saudi Arabia on Saturday 14 November for the Saudi Arabian rally based in Jeddah. It marks round fourteen of the calendar and closes out the season's later stages.

items.headline: NHRA Finals
items.body: The NHRA Finals bring the drag racing season to its conclusion at Pomona Dragstrip in California on Sunday 15 November.

editions.title: Last week on E-Grid
editions.intro: This week ran eight rounds across five championships, from the World Endurance Championship's 8 Hours of Bahrain to Formula 1's Brazilian Grand Prix and NASCAR's championship finale, with MotoGP back at Lusail. Norris, Bezzecchi and Blaney claimed their Sunday wins.

items.headline: 8 Hours of Bahrain
items.body: The World Endurance Championship came to the Bahrain International Circuit for the 8 Hours of Bahrain on Saturday. It was an endurance test across the full distance, where reliability and consistency were as important as raw pace.

items.headline: Portimão
items.detail: Autódromo Internacional do Algarve, Portugal · Sun 8 Nov
items.body: The Clio Cup Series came to the Autódromo Internacional do Algarve for round seven at Portimão on Sunday. It was a full day of single-make racing along the Portuguese coast, with drivers pressing hard for position across a tightly packed field.

items.headline: Brazilian Grand Prix
items.detail: Autódromo José Carlos Pace, Brazil · Sun 8 Nov
items.body: Lando Norris took the Brazilian Grand Prix from pole, finishing 14.6 seconds clear of Max Verstappen with Isack Hadjar third on another Red Bull one-two. Rain fell during the race as Verstappen climbed from 21st to second, while Lewis Hamilton made a steady run up to ninth. Andrea Kimi Antonelli took the fastest lap and saw his championship lead over Verstappen fall from 119 to 111 points.
facts: Lando Norris won from pole, 14.6 seconds ahead of Max Verstappen
Biggest climbers: Max Verstappen from 21st to 2nd and Lewis Hamilton from 20th to 9th
Fastest lap: Andrea Kimi Antonelli, 1:12.689
Did not finish: Lance Stroll and Valtteri Bottas (did not start)
Andrea Kimi Antonelli's championship lead over Max Verstappen went from 119 to 111 points over the weekend
Rain fell during the race

items.headline: Grand Prix of Qatar
items.detail: Lusail International Circuit, Qatar · Sun 8 Nov
items.body: Marco Bezzecchi won the Grand Prix of Qatar from Marc Marquez by 3.1 seconds, with Raul Fernandez third as the season's finale came to Lusail. It was a dry race in 31°C air and 33°C on the track, where Marquez set a new lap record. He had already taken Saturday's sprint, and his championship lead over Jorge Martin grew from 44 to 60 points.
facts: Marco Bezzecchi won by 3.1 seconds from Marc Marquez
Did not finish: Brad Binder and Diogo Moreira
Marc Marquez set a new lap record, 1:52.558
Dry, 31°C air and 33°C track
Saturday's sprint was won by Marc Marquez
Marc Marquez's championship lead over Jorge Martin went from 44 to 60 points this weekend

items.headline: Championship Race
items.body: Ryan Blaney won the NASCAR Championship Race from ninth on the grid at Homestead-Miami Speedway, taking a narrow 0.314-second margin over Tyler Reddick with William Byron third. Kyle Larson's title was decided as his Chase lead over Christopher Bell fell from 67 to 49 points, while Blaney's win lifted him from seventh to fourth in the Chase. Denny Hamlin led the most laps and won stage two.
facts: Ryan Blaney won from 9th on the grid
Most laps led: Denny Hamlin (87)
Stage winners: Stage 1 Tyler Reddick, Stage 2 Denny Hamlin
Margin of victory: 0.314 s

The win lifted Ryan Blaney from 7th to 4th in the Chase

lastRaces.headline: Championship Race
lastRaces.body: Ryan Blaney won from ninth on the grid, holding Tyler Reddick of 23XI Racing for a 0.314-second margin in a 267-lap race in which eight drivers traded the lead. William Byron completed the podium for Hendrick Motorsports behind him, while Larson's Chase edge over Bell fell from 67 to 49 points.

lastRaces.detail: Lusail International Circuit, Qatar · Sun 8 Nov
lastRaces.body: Marco Bezzecchi took the Qatar Grand Prix home by 3.1 seconds over Marc Marquez on a dry, 33°C track where Marquez set a new lap record of 1:52.558. Raul Fernandez made up the podium for SuperFile Trackhouse behind them, and Saturday's sprint had already gone to Marquez as his lead over Jorge Martin grew from 44 to 60 points.

lastRaces.headline: Brazilian Grand Prix
lastRaces.detail: Autódromo José Carlos Pace, Brazil · Sun 8 Nov
lastRaces.body: Lando Norris won from pole by 14.6 seconds over Max Verstappen, with Isack Hadjar third for Red Bull as McLaren and Red Bull filled the top three. Rain fell during the race as Norris made three stops on intermediate, soft, soft then intermediate tyres. Verstappen recovered from 21st to second and Hamilton climbed from 20th to ninth.

lastRaces.headline: Portimão
lastRaces.detail: Autódromo Internacional do Algarve, Portugal · Sun 8 Nov
lastRaces.body: Portimão's round of the Clio Cup Series ran on Sunday across the Autódromo Internacional do Algarve in Portugal. It was a day of touring-car racing that rounded out the week alongside the season's headline events.

lastRaces.headline: 8 Hours of Bahrain
lastRaces.body: The 8 Hours of Bahrain served as round eight of the World Endurance Championship, staged on Saturday 7 November at the Bahrain International Circuit. It was a demanding endurance test that brought the series back to the desert for its latest round.

lastRaces.headline: Las Vegas Nationals
lastRaces.detail: Las Vegas Motor Speedway · Sun 1 Nov
lastRaces.body: The Las Vegas Nationals brought drag racing to Las Vegas Motor Speedway on Sunday 1 November. Drivers lined up across the weekend for a full day of quarter-mile action, chasing speed and consistency down the strip.

lastRaces.headline: Rally Italia Sardegna
lastRaces.body: World Rally Championship's Rally Italia Sardegna came around Alghero in Italy on Sunday 4 October, forming round 13 of the season. It was another demanding test across Sardinia for the leading crews as they pressed on through the latter half of the calendar.

lastRaces.headline: Motul Petit Le Mans
lastRaces.detail: Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta · Sat 3 Oct
lastRaces.body: IMSA's SportsCar Championship reaches its finale with the Motul Petit Le Mans at Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta on Saturday 3 October. The endurance marathon has long stood as the series' crowning event, capping another demanding season of sports car racing.

lastRaces.headline: Baku
lastRaces.detail: Baku City Circuit, Azerbaijan · Sun 27 Sep
lastRaces.body: Formula 2 brought its sprint and feature races to the Baku City Circuit in Azerbaijan on Sunday 27 September. The narrow street track threading the old city's walls offered another tight, technical test for the feeder series.

lastRaces.headline: Madrid
lastRaces.body: Formula 3's tenth round came to Madrid, Spain on Sunday 13 September. The championship's Spanish round brought its racing to the city that weekend.

lastRaces.headline: Monza (double-header)
lastRaces.detail: Autodromo Nazionale Monza, Italy · Sun 6 Sep
lastRaces.body: Autodromo Nazionale Monza has hosted racing since 1922, its 5.793 km lap threading through 11 corners. The Porsche Supercup's seventh round ran here on Sunday 6 September as a double-header in Italy.
facts: 5.793 km lap, 11 corners, first raced 1922

lastRaces.headline: Season Finale
lastRaces.detail: WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca · Sun 6 Sep
lastRaces.body: IndyCar's season finale reached WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca on Sunday 6 September. As the championship's final round of the year, it brought the season to a close at the venue.
